analysis_type: Post-hoc comparison of three existing external candidate stress outputs; no refitting, retuning or new experiment

comparison_rule.driver: Use scripts/external_coverage.py as the single reusable driver and preserve wrapper-specific native-model boundaries
comparison_rule.metrics: Retain dataset-specific total points, ellipsoid-available and unavailable points, covered points, continuous safe folds, bound widths, independent-box status and candidate/baseline RMSE per fold
comparison_rule.totals: Sums describe these 365 observations only: 305 ellipsoid-available points and 60 unavailable points; they are not a universal external success rate or probability coverage
comparison_rule.evidence_levels: All three are candidate approximation stress tests, not native-model validation, physical endogeneity, independent physical experiments or probability calibration
comparison_rule.previous_comparison: Preserve exports/external-coverage-comparison.json and its two-dataset protocol unchanged

limitations: All three candidates are approximation stress tests and not their native model classes
The 365-point descriptive total includes 60 points without an available ellipsoid bound and is not a probability coverage estimate or universal success rate
Gauss1 contributes generated observations, a failed predictive fold and a fold with no ellipsoid bounds; none may be hidden
Different native models, bound widths and independent-box availability remain dataset-specific
Continuous denominator safety and pointwise residual coverage do not guarantee useful prediction or physical endogeneity
